critical_steps: The source family with one operator one-half times the identity has exact controlled K-g-frame bound one quarter.
The zero perturbed family satisfies the printed component perturbation hypothesis with c equal to one half and eta equal to one quarter.
The source formula then produces a positive claimed lower bound one sixteenth although the perturbed energy is identically zero.
For direct square-root differences, l2 aggregation of the c_i term contributes the square root of eta.
Minkowski inequalities give the stated corrected lower and upper bounds under a strictly positive smallness margin.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact one-dimensional specialization plus a direct Hilbert direct-sum Minkowski estimate for the safe replacement theorem.
integrity.unproved_limits: No general equivalence is claimed between the source's square-root-of-operator-difference hypothesis and the direct square-root-difference hypothesis.

scientific_limitations: The counterexample refutes Theorem 4.1 and its zero-relative-parameter specialization Proposition 4.1.

The valid replacement proved here strengthens the perturbation hypothesis to direct differences of positive square roots; it does not assert that the source's original square-root-of-difference hypothesis is repaired in full generality merely by replacing eta with its square root.
An unindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same counterexample or diagnosis.
title: A scalar counterexample to a controlled \(K\)-\(g\)-frame perturbation theorem
